title: Duo Device Trust Posture
exclusions: Covers only devices that authenticate through Duo, and posture detail only where Duo Desktop and the Universal Prompt are in use. It is not a full endpoint inventory; use the endpoint management tool for that.
evidence: Daily report export listing non-compliant devices with posture values, plus the endpoint team's remediation ticket per device.

controlTest.positiveScenario: On a test laptop with Duo Desktop, turn off the host firewall and sign in to a Duo-protected application under a policy that requires a firewall. The attempt is denied with a device-health reason, and the search returns a row for the test user and device with `firewall=false`.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Turn the firewall back on and sign in again. The attempt succeeds with no posture reason and all posture fields true, and the device no longer appears in the results for that window.

dataSources: `index=duo sourcetype=cisco:duo:authentication_v2` from the Cisco Security Cloud (7404) Duo input, Authentication log type, which polls `GET /admin/v2/logs/authentication`. One JSON event per authentication or enrollment attempt with `event_type`, `result`, `reason`, `factor`, `user.name`, `application.name`, `access_device.*`, and `auth_device.*`.
app: Cisco Security Cloud (`CiscoSecurityCloud`, [Splunkbase 7404](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/7404)), Cisco Duo input. Replaces the deprecated Duo Splunk Connector (Splunkbase 3504, end of life 31 May 2026).
spl:
index=duo sourcetype="cisco:duo:authentication_v2" event_type="authentication"
| eval result=lower(result), user=coalesce('user.name', username)
| rename access_device.hostname as device_host, access_device.os as os, access_device.os_version as os_version, access_device.is_encryption_enabled as encryption, access_device.is_firewall_enabled as firewall, access_device.is_password_set as password_set
| where in(reason, "endpoint_is_not_trusted", "endpoint_is_not_in_management_system", "endpoint_is_not_healthy", "endpoint_failed_duo_desktop_verification", "health_requirements_not_met", "no_disk_encryption", "no_screen_lock", "rooted_device", "out_of_date") OR encryption="false" OR firewall="false" OR password_set="false"
| stats count as attempts values(result) as results values(reason) as reasons latest(encryption) as encryption latest(firewall) as firewall latest(password_set) as password_set latest(os_version) as os_version by user device_host os
| sort - attempts
description: Lists users and devices whose Duo authentications were denied for a device-trust reason, or that signed in from a device Duo Desktop reports as unencrypted, firewall-off, or without a system password. Each row shows the device, its OS, the posture values, and whether access was granted.
value: Device trust only protects you if the failures are worked. This report shows which users are blocked by posture checks and, more importantly, which unhealthy devices still got in because the policy only warns, so the endpoint team can fix the device and the identity team can decide when to enforce.
implementation: Collect the Duo Authentication log (v2) with the Cisco Security Cloud (7404) Duo input into `index=duo`. Install Duo Desktop on managed endpoints and enable the Duo Universal Prompt so posture fields are filled. Run daily as a report, and alert only on `results=success` rows for users in privileged groups.
visualization: Table: user, device_host, os, os_version, encryption, firewall, password_set, reasons, results, attempts. Supporting panels: posture failures by reason over 30 days (stacked column), share of authentications with each posture field false (single values).

references.title: Cisco Security Cloud App for Splunk User Guide

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Devices without Duo Desktop** — `access_device.is_*` fields are "unknown", not "false", when Duo Desktop is absent, so those devices only appear through a denial reason. Missing posture is not a failed posture.

2. **Encryption still in progress** — a new laptop reports `is_encryption_enabled=false` until BitLocker or FileVault finishes. Recheck after 24 hours.

3. **Lab and kiosk devices** — shared devices may be exempt from posture policy by design. Keep them in a lookup with an owner.

**Suppression:** a lookup of exempt device hostnames, applied after `stats`.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Cisco Security Cloud (`CiscoSecurityCloud`, Splunkbase 7404) on the search heads and on the heavy forwarder or Splunk Cloud Inputs Data Manager that runs its modular inputs. It replaces the Duo Splunk Connector (Splunkbase 3504, end of life 31 May 2026); disable the old connector's inputs after cutover so events are not indexed twice.
• A Duo Admin API application created by an Owner-role administrator in the Duo Admin Panel under Applications > Protect an Application > Admin API. Record the integration key, secret key, and API hostname (`api-XXXXXXXX.duosecurity.com`), and grant it **Grant read log**.
• Outbound HTTPS (TCP 443) from the input host to the API hostname, and an accurate system clock on that host, because the Admin API signs every request with the current date.
• An index for Duo data (this page uses `index=duo`) and a role with `srchIndexesAllowed` on it for the identity and SOC teams.
• Duo Premier or Duo Advantage, because device-health fields and Trusted Endpoints are not returned on other plans.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
• In Cisco Security Cloud open Application Setup, choose the Cisco Duo card, and create an input with the integration key, secret key, and API hostname. Enable the Authentication log type (the v2 endpoint, not Authentication Legacy v1) and set the index to `duo`.
• The input reads `GET /admin/v2/logs/authentication` and writes `sourcetype=cisco:duo:authentication_v2`. `result` is one of `success`, `denied`, `failure`, `error`, or `fraud` in lowercase; the legacy v1 type `cisco:duo:authentication` uses uppercase values, so the searches lowercase `result` before comparing.
• Device-posture fields under `access_device` (`is_encryption_enabled`, `is_firewall_enabled`, `is_password_set`, `security_agents`) are filled only when the application uses the Duo Universal Prompt and Duo Desktop is installed, and only on Duo Premier or Advantage plans.
• Check the fields this search needs: run `index=duo sourcetype=cisco:duo:authentication_v2 | stats count by access_device.is_encryption_enabled access_device.is_firewall_enabled` over 7 days and confirm values other than "unknown" appear.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=duo sourcetype="cisco:duo:authentication_v2" event_type="authentication"
| eval result=lower(result), user=coalesce('user.name', username)
| rename access_device.hostname as device_host, access_device.os as os, access_device.os_version as os_version, access_device.is_encryption_enabled as encryption, access_device.is_firewall_enabled as firewall, access_device.is_password_set as password_set
| where in(reason, "endpoint_is_not_trusted", "endpoint_is_not_in_management_system", "endpoint_is_not_healthy", "endpoint_failed_duo_desktop_verification", "health_requirements_not_met", "no_disk_encryption", "no_screen_lock", "rooted_device", "out_of_date") OR encryption="false" OR firewall="false" OR password_set="false"
| stats count as attempts values(result) as results values(reason) as reasons latest(encryption) as encryption latest(firewall) as firewall latest(password_set) as password_set latest(os_version) as os_version by user device_host os
| sort - attempts
```

Understanding this SPL
• The first line limits the search to authentication attempts in the v2 log.
• `rename` gives the nested `access_device` posture fields short names for the `where` and `stats` clauses.
• The `reason` list is the Duo denial reasons that come from device trust and health checks; the posture comparisons catch devices that were allowed even though a check failed, which happens when the policy only warns.
• Duo writes posture as the strings `true`, `false`, or `unknown`, so the comparison is against the string "false".
• `stats` per user, device, and OS keeps the latest posture values, so the row shows the device's current state.

Step 3 — Validate
• Compare with the Duo admin console (Admin Panel) under Reports > Authentication Log for the same user and time range: each attempt listed there should appear in `index=duo` with the same result and reason.
• Open one listed device in the Admin Panel under Endpoints and confirm its encryption, firewall, and password state match the row.
• Run `index=duo sourcetype=cisco:duo:authentication_v2 | timechart span=1h count by result` over 7 days; gaps longer than two input intervals point to collection failures, not quiet periods.

Step 4 — Operationalize
• Run daily over the last 24 hours and email the report to the endpoint team.
• Alert separately on rows where `results` contains `success` and the user is in a privileged group lookup; those are unhealthy devices with admin access.
• Track the share of authentications with a false posture field each month, and use it to decide when to switch the policy from warn to block.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• No Duo events and HTTP 401 in the input log under `$SPLUNK_HOME/var/log/splunk/duo_splunkapp/`: wrong secret key, an API hostname from a different Duo account, or clock skew on the input host.
• HTTP 403: the Admin API application is missing **Grant read log**.
• HTTP 429: Duo rate-limits the log endpoints. Make sure the deprecated 3504 connector and the 7404 input are not both polling the same Admin API application.
• Duplicate rows after migration: the 3504 connector and the 7404 input are both enabled for the same log type.
• Searches return nothing but events exist: the input is on Authentication Legacy v1, so events are in `cisco:duo:authentication` with uppercase `result` and flat `username`. Switch the input to the v2 log type rather than editing the searches.
• Missing fields `user.name` or `access_device.ip`: the events were indexed before `KV_MODE=json` applied, or a custom props stanza overrides the add-on. Check `| fieldsummary` on one hour of data.
• Posture fields are always "unknown": Duo Desktop is not installed or the application uses the traditional prompt. Check the Endpoints page in the Admin Panel.
grandmaExplanation: We list the computers and phones that tried to log in without basic protections like a screen password or disk encryption, so they get fixed.
